  return <><_components.h1>{"Few-Shot Prompting"}</_components.h1>{"\n"}{"\n"}<iframe width="100%" height="415px" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/ojtbHUqw1LA?si=DPHurHTzZXm22vcN" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowFullScreen />{"\n"}<_components.p>{"While large-language models demonstrate remarkable zero-shot capabilities, they still fall short on more complex tasks when using the zero-shot setting. Few-shot prompting can be used as a technique to enable in-context learning where we provide demonstrations in the prompt to steer the model to better performance. The demonstrations serve as conditioning for subsequent examples where we would like the model to generate a response."}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"According to "}<_components.a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.13971.pdf">{"Touvron et al. 2023"}</_components.a>{" few shot properties first appeared when models were scaled to a sufficient size "}<_components.a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08361">{"(Kaplan et al., 2020)"}</_components.a>{"."}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"Let's demonstrate few-shot prompting via an example that was presented in "}<_components.a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165">{"Brown et al. 2020"}</_components.a>{".     color: "var(--shiki-color-text)"

    color: "var(--shiki-color-text)"

    color: "var(--shiki-color-text)"

    color: "var(--shiki-color-text)"
  }}>{"When we won the game, we all started to farduddle in celebration."}</_components.span></_components.span></_components.code></_components.pre>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"We can observe that the model has somehow learned how to perform the task by providing it with just one example (i.e., 1-shot). For more difficult tasks, we can experiment with increasing the demonstrations (e.g., 3-shot, 5-shot, 10-shot, etc.)."}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"Following the findings from "}<_components.a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.12837">{"Min et al. (2022)"}</_components.a>{", here are a few more tips about demonstrations/exemplars when doing few-shot:"}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"\"the label space and the distribution of the input text specified by the demonstrations are both important (regardless of whether the labels are correct for individual inputs)\""}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"the format you use also plays a key role in performance, even if you just use random labels, this is much better than no labels at all."}</_components.li>{"\n"}<_components.li>{"additional results show that selecting random labels from a true distribution of labels (instead of a uniform distribution) also helps."}</_components.li>{"\n"}</_components.ul>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"Let's try out a few examples. If you take a closer look, the type of task we have introduced involves a few more reasoning steps. In other words, it might help if we break the problem down into steps and demonstrate that to the model. More recently, "}<_components.a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11903">{"chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting"}</_components.a>{" has been popularized to address more complex arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks."}</_components.p>{"\n"}<_components.p>{"Overall, it seems that providing examples is useful for solving some tasks.
